text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
BARLEY TENDER - Saudi Arabia will tender on Tuesday for one million tonnes of feed barley of optional origin, European grain traders said. The barley is for delivery in September and October.

SOYBEAN TENDER - Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association will tender on Tuesday for a 54,000-tonne shipment of Brazilian or Argentine soybeans, traders said. The shipment is slated for delivery from a South American port between August 21 to September 10, traders said.

WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC said it was seeking up to 42,000 tonnes of U.S. no.2 or better hard red winter wheat under its export program for Ethiopia. The shipment period was set July 15-July 30. Offers were due on June 26.

- Pakistan is tendering on June 25 for 500,000 tonnes of optional origin white wheat, July 11-August 10 shipment, a spokesman at the country's U.S. embassy in Washington said. He said the wheat would be either from the United States, Australia or Canada.

WHEAT TENDERS (cont.) - The Cyprus Grain Commission on Wednesday invited tenders for the supply of 12,000 tonnes of soft bread making wheat, a statement from the commission said. Shipment period is scheduled between July 15 and 30, 1997. The tender closing date is Tuesday, June 24.

PALM OIL TENDER - Egypt's official Holding Company for Food Industries was seeking 25,000 tonnes of Malaysian and/or Indonesian palm stearin and palm oil for delivery in August. The deadline for bids was 0900 GMT on June 25. The oils were in the following lots: -- 10,000 tonnes of palm stearin and 15,000 tonnes of palm oil.
MARKET TALK - China's corn exports should remain slack for the rest of 1997, with sporadic sales to the Philippines and Vietnam likely to be the only activity.
Japanese and South Korean buyers are ready to buy U.S. corn if corn premiums or freight rates fall further, traders said Monday.

South Korean feed millers and crushers are expected to buy soybeans and soymeal this week for their fourth quarter requirements, prompted by recent sharp declines in Chicago futures, traders said Monday.
